DayZ Admin Commands: BattlEye RCon and Admin Tools

notes: DayZ speaks BattlEye RCon (BERCon), not Source RCON: it is a UDP protocol with its own login/packet/CRC framing, configured in BEServer_x64.cfg (Windows) / beserver_x64.cfg (Linux) next to the BE server module, relocatable with -BEpath=. PORT: since DayZ 1.13 there is NO default RCon port - if RConPort is unset BattlEye binds a random port (Bohemia feedback T159179, closed as intended), and the pre-1.13 behaviour of using the game port or game port + 2 no longer works. 2306 is recorded as defaultPort because it is the convention hosts and tools ship with; CFTools instead recommends game port + 3 (2305). Always read RConPort from the config rather than trusting 2306. IDENTIFIER: BattlEye kick and ban take the PLAYER NUMBER - the [#] column of 'players' - not a GUID, so the roster must be refreshed immediately before acting; the number is session-scoped and is reused after a disconnect. 'ban <player #> <minutes> <reason>' bans that player's BE GUID (0 or omitted = permanent). To ban someone who is offline use 'addBan <GUID or IP> <minutes> <reason>' with the 32-hex BE GUID from the roster's accountId. UNBAN: BattlEye's removeBan takes a BAN INDEX from the 'bans' listing, not a player id or GUID, so it cannot be expressed as a {playerId} template and both unban and banList.liveUnban are omitted - unban by reading 'bans', matching the GUID, then sending 'removeBan <ban #>' and 'writeBans'. 'writeBans' flushes the in-memory list to bans.txt and drops expired entries; 'loadBans' reloads it. No server-info command exists in BE RCon ('version' only reports the BE server build), so info is omitted, and there is no MOTD command. RestrictRCon 1 in the BE config limits RCon to a reduced command set - set it to 0 for full kick/ban control. Disagreement: XGamingServer's DayZ doc calls the RCon port TCP; BattlEye RCon is UDP. Separately, serverDZ.cfg has disableBanlist and a DayZ-level ban.txt of Steam64 IDs, which is a different list from BattlEye's GUID-based bans.txt recorded here.
